pois.name: Twierdza Wisłoujście
pois.intro: Wisłoujście Fortress is a historic fortress located in Gdańsk by the Martwa Wisła river, by an old estuary of the river Vistula, flowing into the Bay of Gdańsk. The fortress is located close to the Wisłoujście borough, Westerplatte and the Port Północny.

pois.name: Pomnik Obrońców Wybrzeża
pois.description: Granitowy, 25-metrowy obelisk w kształcie wyszczerbionego bagnetu na szczycie kopca.
pois.intro: The Westerplatte Monument, also known as the Monument to the Defenders of the Coast is a war memorial located in Gdańsk, Poland, on the Westerplatte Peninsula in the Gdańsk harbour channel constructed between 1964–1966 to commemorate the Polish defenders of the Military Transit Depot in the Battle of Westerplatte, one of the first battles in Germany's invasion of Poland, which marked the outbreak...

pois.name: Latarnia Morska Gdańsk Nowy Port
pois.intro: Der Leuchtturm Gdańsk Nowy Port, benannt nach dem gleichnamigen Stadtbezirk, ist ein Leuchtturm an der Ostsee und zeigte bis 1984 den Schiffen die Einfahrt in den Hafen der Seestadt Danzig, in der polnischen Woiwodschaft Pommern. Benachbarte Leuchttürme stehen in Hel und in Krynica Morska im Westen.

pois.name: Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk
pois.intro: The Gdańsk Stadium, known for sponsorship reasons as the Polsat Plus Arena Gdańsk since May 2021, is a football stadium in Gdańsk, Pomeranian Voivodeship, Poland. It is used mostly for football matches and is the home stadium of Lechia Gdańsk, which competes in the I liga, and the Poland women's national football team.

pois.name: Westerplatte
pois.intro: Westerplatte is a peninsula in Gdańsk, Poland, located on the Baltic Sea coast mouth of the Dead Vistula, in the Gdańsk harbour channel. From 1926 to 1939, it was the location of a Polish Military Transit Depot, sanctioned within the territory of the Free City of Danzig.

pois.name: Muzeum II Wojny Światowej
pois.nameEnglish: Museum of the Second World War
pois.wikipedia: pl:Muzeum II Wojny Światowej w Gdańsku
pois.intro: The Museum of the Second World War is a state cultural institution and museum established in 2008 in Gdańsk, Poland, which is devoted to the Second World War. Its exhibits opened in 2017.

pois.name: Krzywy Domek
pois.intro: Krzywy Domek is an unusually shaped building in Sopot, Poland. Krzywy Domek was built in 2004.

pois.name: Ratusz Głównego Miasta
pois.intro: Main City Hall is a historic town hall located in Gdańsk, Poland, within the Main City borough of the Downtown district. It is one of the finest examples of the Gothic-Renaissance historic buildings in the city, built at the intersection of Ulica Długa and Długi Targ, in the most popular part of Gdańsk.

pois.name: Bazylika Archikatedralna Trójcy Świętej
pois.intro: Oliwa Cathedral, formally known as the Archcathedral Basilica of the Holy Trinity, is a Roman Catholic church in the district of Oliwa, in Gdańsk, Poland. Completed in the late 14th century in a Brick Gothic style, the present church comprises Mannerist-Baroque architectural elements.

pois.name: Dworzec PKP Gdańsk Główny
pois.intro: Gdańsk Główny is the chief railway station serving the city of Gdańsk, in the Pomeranian Voivodeship, Poland. The station opened in 1900 and is located on the Warsaw–Gdańsk railway, Gdańsk–Stargard railway, the parallel Gdańsk Śródmieście–Rumia railway, Gdańsk Główny–Gdańsk Zaspa Towarowa railway and Gdańsk Główny–Gdańsk Nowy Port railway.

pois.name: Europejskie Centrum Solidarności
pois.intro: The European Solidarity Centre is a museum and library in Gdańsk, Poland, devoted to the history of Solidarity, the Polish trade union and civil resistance movement, and other opposition movements of Communist Eastern Europe. It opened on 31 August 2014.

pois.name: Narodowe Muzeum Morskie
pois.intro: The National Maritime Museum in Gdańsk is a maritime museum in Gdańsk, Poland, established on 1 January 1962.

pois.name: Pomnik Poległych Stoczniowców 1970
pois.intro: The Monument to the Fallen Shipyard Workers 1970 was unveiled on 16 December 1980 near the entrance to what was then the Lenin Shipyard in Gdańsk, on the Baltic coast of northern Poland. It commemorates the 42 or more people killed during the Coastal cities events in December 1970.

pois.name: Brama Żuraw
pois.intro: The Gdańsk Crane or the Crane Gate is a 15th-century crane located in central Gdańsk, Poland, on the Motława river. One of the city's most well-known structures and tourist attractions, it was the largest port crane in medieval Europe and is presently found on the regional heritage list.

pois.name: Muzeum Narodowe w Gdańsku
pois.intro: The National Museum in Gdańsk, established in 1972 in Gdańsk, is one of the main branches of Poland's national museum system.

pois.name: Złota Brama
pois.intro: The Golden Gate is a historic Renaissance city gate in Gdańsk, Poland. It is located within the Royal Route, the most prominent part of the Old Town and is one of its most notable tourist attractions.

pois.name: Fontanna Neptuna
pois.intro: Neptune's Fountain is a historic fountain in Gdańsk, a Mannerist-Rococo masterpiece, and one of the most distinctive landmarks of the city. The fountain is located at the Długi Targ, in front of the entrance to the Artus Court.

pois.name: Ośrodek Kultury Morskiej
pois.intro: The National Maritime Museum in Gdańsk is a maritime museum in Gdańsk, Poland, established on 1 January 1962.

pois.name: Dom Uphagena
pois.intro: The Uphagen House is a reconstructed 18th-century merchant house in Gdańsk, Poland, located at the Ulica Długa within the Royal Route in the historic Main City. It houses a museum, which is a branch of the local historical museum.

pois.name: Dwór Artusa
pois.intro: The Artus Court is a building in the centre of Gdańsk at Długi Targ 44, which used to be the meeting place of merchants and a centre of social life. Today it is a point of interest of numerous visitors and a branch of the Gdańsk History Museum.

pois.name: Latarnia morska Gdańsk Port Północny
pois.intro: Gdańsk Port Północny Lighthouse is a lighthouse in Gdańsk, located on the Polish coast of the Baltic Sea, by the Bay of Gdańsk. It is the youngest lighthouse in Poland; located between the lighthouse in Hel, and the lighthouse in Krynica Morska.

pois.name: Bazylika Świętej Brygidy
pois.intro: Die Brigittenkirche befindet sich in der Danziger Altstadt in der Ulica Profesorska und grenzt östlich an den Kirchhof der Katharinenkirche und den Radaunekanal.

pois.name: Sala BHP
pois.intro: Die Arbeitsschutzhalle der Danziger Werft ist ein Gebäude auf dem Areal der ehemaligen Kaiserlichen Werft Danzig. Ihr polnischer Name lautet Sala BHP, wegen ihrer ursprünglichen Funktion ist sie auch als Torpedohalle der Danziger Werft bekannt.

pois.name: Bazylika Świętego Mikołaja
pois.intro: Basilica of Saint Nicholas is a Brick Gothic church situated in the Old Town of Gdańsk, Poland.

pois.name: Forum Gdańsk
pois.description: Położona w rejonie starówki jasna, przestronna nowoczesna galeria handlowa ze sklepami światowych marek i ok. 20 restauracjami.
pois.intro: Forum Gdańsk, often shortened to Forum is a Polish shopping mall located in Gdańsk and opened in 2018.

pois.name: Galeria Bałtycka
pois.intro: Die Baltische Galerie ist ein Einkaufszentrum in Danzig-Langfuhr. Sie liegt ziemlich zentral und erreicht in ihrem Einzugsgebiet rund 1.200.000 Einwohner.

pois.name: Galeria Handlowa Madison
pois.intro: Madison – galeria handlowa w Gdańsku, na Starym Mieście przy ul. Rajskiej 10.

pois.name: Gdański Ogród Zoologiczny
pois.intro: The Gdańsk Zoo is a zoological garden located in Gdańsk, Pomeranian Voivodship, Poland. It was opened in the district of Oliwa in 1954 and covers 123.76 hectares, which makes it the largest zoological garden in Poland in terms of area.

pois.name: Park Oliwski im. Adama Mickiewicza
pois.intro: Park Oliwa of Adam Mickiewicz Park is een park in de wijk Oliwa in de Poolse stad Gdańsk. Het park is erkend als monument.

pois.name: Park imienia Ronalda Reagana
pois.intro: The Ronald Reagan Park is located in the neighborhood of Przymorze Wielkie, Gdańsk, Poland. Built between 2003 and 2006 out of formerly barren lands, it covers 40 hectares.

pois.name: Królewskie Wzgórze
pois.intro: The Królewskie Wzgórze, known before 1945 as Królewska Góra in Polish and Königshöhe in German and now also known as Ślimak and Sobótka, is a 99.2-metre-high hill in Gdańsk in Poland. It is located in the suburb of Wrzeszcz and was originally named after Frederick William III of Prussia.

pois.description: Punkt widokowy z cyklu „Spojrzenie na Gdańsk”

pois.name: Park Kuźniczki
pois.intro: Park Kuźniczki – zabytkowy niewielki park w Gdańsku, na obszarze dzielnicy Wrzeszcz.

pois.name: Polska Filharmonia Bałtycka im. Fryderyka Chopina
pois.intro: Polish Baltic F. Chopin Philharmonic in Gdańsk is a concert hall located in Ołowianka, Gdańsk.

pois.name: Kościół pw. Świętej Katarzyny
pois.intro: St Catherine's Church is the oldest church in Gdańsk, Poland.

pois.name: Brama Zielona
pois.intro: The Green Gate in Gdańsk, Poland, is one of the city's most notable tourist attractions. It is situated between Long Market and the River Motława.

pois.name: Międzynarodowe Stowarzyszenie Bursztynników
pois.intro: Międzynarodowe Stowarzyszenie Bursztynników – jedyna organizacja non-profit na świecie zrzeszająca projektantów, producentów biżuterii, właścicieli galerii, naukowców, badaczy, gemmologów, muzealników, kolekcjonerów i handlowców wyrobami z bursztynem bałtyckim.

terminalResolution.notes: The Westerplatte cruise quay takes smaller ships; most large ships call at Gdynia instead.
